leading_positions.synthesis: All eight members state B005 (optical lattice clocks, Katori and Ye) as a one-part preferred configuration. Eight of eight give the same two laureates and a citation about the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks and a new regime of precision measurement; Danielsson, Johansson and Lindroth add time/frequency or the 10^-18 level to the wording. Three members (Eriksson, Johansson, Pearce) moved to B005 from a different opening first choice, and Mehlig moved from a first choice (B016) that no colleague supports. What is shared is the scientific core (magic-wavelength trapping, many atoms in the Lamb-Dicke regime, about 1e-18 uncertainty, independent reproduction) and the two-name attribution. What is not shared is how much weight the overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes and the pending SI second redefinition deserve. Each member lists a different set of alternatives (B035 and B014 most often, then B015, B016 and B051), and none of these is part of any member's preferred configuration.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members place B005 alone in their preferred configuration with Hidetoshi Katori and Jun Ye as the two laureates; no member proposes a different or third name for this ballot.

Members describe the scientific core in the same terms: a magic-wavelength lattice removes motional and light-shift errors while thousands of neutral atoms are interrogated, reaching roughly 1e-18 fractional uncertainty.

Members cite independent reproduction and clock comparisons at JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE and others as evidence of maturity, and name tests of constants, dark-matter searches and relativistic geodesy as physical payoffs.

Members agree that the citation should be written narrowly around the lattice-clock invention and realization and not around precision metrology or the frequency comb in general (stated explicitly by Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce in their responses).

All eight record, in their own case_against, the reservation about overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes and about credit outside the two names (Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley, Lemonde and others); all except Pearce also raise the pending SI second redefinition.
scientific_disputes: Whether the lattice clock is a discovery or invention distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-control prizes, or an excellent refinement of that lineage. Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce raise this; Mehlig says it is answerable but not settled; Eriksson explicitly asks whether the many-atom lattice step is a real conceptual advance over single-ion clocks or mainly a gain in averaging.

Whether a precision-measurement advance counts as a discovery in the Nobel sense. Mehlig and Olsson raise the discovery-versus-engineering question; Kroll states he does not treat precision measurement as a lesser category.

Whether the clean 1e-18 results suffice or whether a measured variation of a constant or a violation has to be found for the physics to be considered decisive (Danielsson notes that only tightened bounds have been obtained so far).

Which alternative, if any, should sit beside or replace B005: B035 (Danielsson, Kroll, Pearce), B014 (Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson, Pearce), B015 (Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth), B016 (Mehlig) and B051 (Olsson). The alternatives reflect different views on whether a second, distinct physics discovery should be sought, and none is in any preferred configuration.
attribution_disputes: Priority between Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and parallel lattice-clock ideas and early demonstrations; Danielsson, Olsson and Pearce say they cannot verify the chronology from the supplied text, and Olsson asks that Katori's 2001-2003 proposal be checked against the first strontium lattice-clock measurements.

Whether Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley, Lemonde, Derevianko and other contributors have a claim that a Katori and Ye pairing cannot represent. Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce each raise some version of this; Johansson asks whether a third name is justified, which the credited list does not allow.
Whether the ion-clock and neutral-atom clock lineages are sufficiently separated in the credited names (Johansson, Kroll, Mehlig).

For the alternatives, the credit questions are different: IceCube (B035) has Halzen, Karle and Spiering inside a collaboration of several hundred people with earlier AMANDA, Baikal and DUMAND history (Olsson, Pearce, Danielsson); B015 has a four-way allocation among Bloch, Greiner, Zoller and Esslinger, with Zoller's separate candidacy (B024) unresolved (Johansson, Lindroth, Eriksson); B014 omits Yuan Cao and other experimental groups (Eriksson).
maturity_disputes: Whether to wait for the formal redefinition of the SI second before awarding B005, or whether the demonstrated 1e-18 performance and independent reproductions already suffice. Danielsson, Eriksson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Olsson list this as a reservation or open point; Eriksson also notes the pending redefinition could make the timing good, and Mehlig asks whether waiting adds maturity or only delay.

For B035, whether TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068 and the Galactic plane results are firm enough; Olsson ranked it sixth for this reason and Pearce moved off it as first choice, while Pearce notes the 2013 discovery is now over a decade old.
For B014, whether the superconducting pairing mechanism must be settled first (Eriksson), and Mehlig's own maturity note on B014.
For B043, whether a computational method counts as a physical discovery given the 1998 chemistry prize for DFT (Eriksson, Lindroth).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Pearce (chair): membership in the PAMELA, Fermi-LAT and XL-Calibur collaborations and an astroparticle field adjacent to IceCube (B035); not an IceCube member, and no direct tie to the credited names; no conflict flagged for B005.
Olsson: field of electron microscopy makes her an interested party on B051 (Rose, Urban, Haider); she would recuse on B051 if it advances. No specific connection to Katori or Ye.

Johansson: directs the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology; possible recusal issue for B046 (circuit QED) and superconducting-circuit candidates, none of which is on the shortlist. No conflict flagged for B005 or B015.

Kroll: an early PhD year in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, a distant connection to the 2005 comb prize, not to Katori or Ye; his WACQT role overlaps institutionally with Johansson's Chalmers home.

Lindroth: close collaborator of Anne L'Huillier (2023 laureate), with ties to the Lund and ETH attosecond groups and to Reinhold Schuch and Paul Indelicato; none involves the shortlisted names, though her closeness to the atomic-physics community around B015 is noted.
Eriksson: ranked B043 (Car-Parrinello) first and notes such methods are part of the computational toolchain in his field; no personal tie to Car or Parrinello.

Mehlig: research is in non-equilibrium statistical physics, near B016 (KPZ), with no recorded collaboration with Kardar, Zhang or Spohn; institutional proximity to Johansson and Olsson in the Gothenburg environment.
Danielsson: no specific conflict; his former supervisor and a frequent co-author are not credited on any shortlisted ballot.
questions_for_round2: Can the committee state in one sentence what the magic-wavelength lattice adds beyond the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 ion-control prize, including whether the many-atom lattice is a conceptual advance over single-ion clocks and not only a gain in averaging?
Can the citation be drafted so that it is narrowly tied to the invention and realization of optical lattice clocks, without suggesting a repeated reward for the comb or for metrology in general?

Should the committee wait for the redefinition of the SI second, or do the demonstrated 1e-18 performance, independent reproductions and clock comparisons already supply the maturity needed? What would change the answer?

Is Katori and Ye the right pair given the priority chronology and the contributions of Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley, Lemonde and Derevianko, and which primary-source checks (Katori's 2001-2003 proposal, first strontium lattice-clock measurements, Ye's record accuracy results) should be requested from outside experts?

If the committee wants a second part or a stronger alternative, which of B035, B014 or B015 is most mature and best bounded in attribution, and what specific information (outside expert views on IceCube roles, treatment of Cao in B014, Zoller and Esslinger in B015) would be needed to decide?

Would members who named B035 as an alternative (Danielsson, Kroll, Pearce) support a two-part prize that pairs B005 with only a subset of Halzen, Karle and Spiering, as Pearce's own statement asks, or does the committee regard that as unfair to the omitted names?
summary.chair_observation: The eight round-1 files converge on a single configuration, B005 with Katori and Ye, and all eight state the same overlap, credit and timing reservations in their own words, so the open points are about how heavily to weigh these reservations and what verification is needed, not about who should be named or which candidate leads. The alternatives are diverse and unsupported by a second shared preferred configuration. Because only explicit round-1 positions are counted, this summary draws no conclusion about final ballots.
